LESSON: WRITING 5.3.1: FUNCTIONAL WRITING: SHOPPING LIST

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 5
Topic 5.3: Writing 5.3.1: Functional Writing: Shopping List
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 5.3.1: Functional Writing: Shopping List, part of Strand 5 in Grade 5 INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES.

Key inquiry question: Why is a shopping list important?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. highlight the format of a shopping list,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 5.3.1: Functional Writing: Shopping List in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. write a shopping list for life-long learning,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 5.3.1: Functional Writing: Shopping List in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. enjoy personal writing for communication.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 5.3.1: Functional Writing: Shopping List in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. highlight the format of a shopping list,

   Writing 5.3.1: Functional Writing: Shopping List helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. write a shopping list for life-long learning,

   Writing 5.3.1: Functional Writing: Shopping List helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. enjoy personal writing for communication.

   Writing 5.3.1: Functional Writing: Shopping List helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. work collaboratively to search for varied samples of shopping lists from print and non-print sources,

2. make notes on the components of a shopping list,

3. describe things to be bought using aspects such as colour, amount, material, shape, size (adjectives),

4. work jointly with peers to write a shopping list for an event based on the theme,

5. present the shopping list in class for peer review,

6. organise the shopping lists in the class portfolio for reference.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. work collaboratively to search for varied samples of shopping lists from print and non-print sources,
2. make notes on the components of a shopping list,
3. describe things to be bought using aspects such as colour, amount, material, shape, size (adjectives),
4. work jointly with peers to write a shopping list for an event based on the theme,
5. present the shopping list in class for peer review,
6. organise the shopping lists in the class portfolio for reference.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 5.3.1: Functional Writing: Shopping List together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and Collaboration: This is enhanced as the learner contributes to group decision making when working with

peers to write a shopping list for an event.

• Learning to Learn: This is developed as the learner is motivated to learn continuously by presenting their shopping lists in

class for peer review.

Values:
• Responsibility: This is developed as the learner cooperates with peers to organise the shopping lists in the class portfolio for

reference.

• Respect: This is enhanced as the learner appreciates and gives positive comments to peers during the review session.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Financial literacy: This is promoted as the learner appreciates the importance of budgeting by preparing shopping lists

ahead of making purchases.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner can relate the concept of shopping lists to their learning of money in Mathematics.
